subtype: Approach: rehearsing a calm, respectful message [Action]
passage: For a week I practised in front of the bathroom mirror, which sounds silly. My wife's father, Divyansh, hosts lunch every Sunday, and we needed to make it every other one, because our weekends had become the only time we saw our own friends. I wrote three lines on a card: I feel stretched, I love those lunches, would every second Sunday work? No "you always". I waited until Divyansh was alone on the veranda with his tea, away from everyone. I thanked him first for the food and the stories. He listened, rubbed his moustache, and said he had been thinking the lunches were too much work for his wife anyway. I had not expected that. My hands were shaking, but he did not get defensive. - Arnab

qa.q: Where did Arnab speak to Divyansh?
qa.a: On the veranda, when Divyansh was alone with his tea.

qa.q: What do Arnab's shaking hands suggest?
qa.a: They suggest nervousness: Arnab was anxious about how Divyansh would react even though the words were practised.

qa.q: What could Arnab try if Divyansh had reacted defensively?
qa.a: Arnab could pause, repeat the thanks, and offer a trial of a few weeks, so the change feels smaller and less like a rejection.

qa.q: How might Divyansh have felt hearing the message on the veranda?
qa.a: Divyansh may have felt respected, since he was thanked first and asked privately, which could explain why he stayed calm and shared his own thought about the work of cooking.

grounding: Arnab prepares a calm, thankful message with I-statements and chooses a private moment to raise the Sunday lunches.
